issue: The review target containment check compares scope paths against the raw reviewTarget text. A files target written as a glob is in contract: deep-review.yaml lines 793-797 say 'Expand glob patterns from review_target', and the expanded list is stored as reviewScopeFiles (yaml line 874). Containment only consults that list for commit ranges (line 405), so with a glob target like 'src/**/*.ts' no scope path equals the target or starts with it plus '/'. Every seed and admission proposal that carries a path scope is pruned as 'relevance'. seedNodes returns admitted: [] with no warning, and the expansive review runs at its loop default with an empty frontier. A '.' target prunes the same way, while a './' target normalizes to blank and allows every scope. Fix: when the target is a pattern or names the repo root, test containment against reviewScopeFiles through scopeInsideTouchedFiles, as commit ranges already do. Keep the change on the target side: mapping '.' to blank in the shared normalizer would break the new test asserting that scope '.' is outside the target.

So `git diff 21c4b325b5a HEAD` changes 64 non-spec files that scope.json leaves out. I replayed the mechanical checks by hand, and they are clean. comment hygiene exit 0 and quality-gate NO_BLOCKER_FOUND over the 45 code files. The 25 runtime test files pass (578 pass, 2 skipped). The 3 system-spec-kit cli test files pass (18). The env reads they add are test-only (DEEP_RESEARCH_PACK_TEMPLATE) or Claude Code's own CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, set on the child. What remains unreviewed is the S1 judgment lens on these files: correctness, a test for each changed behavior, and fail-closed paths. This is an omission, not a false statement. Commit cec5a403eb3 changed how upsert.cjs maps a reused review finding id. The iteration's own derived findings now register in knownFindings before the stored ones (upsert.cjs lines 386-393), so when a reused id splits to finding:<id>#<iteration>, the leaf-sent FINDING node and every edge naming that id land on the new split node, not on the earlier finding. A leaf finding node that folds onto a derived finding now stores { ...derivedMetadata, ...leafMetadata } (lines 444-457), so it gains the derived finding_id, file and line it left out, and a later reused-id check can still compare files. Lines 33-37 still hold: leaf keys win, and the fold targets the node the finding is stored under. But the entry never says that the leaf's node and edges follow the split, or that a folded leaf finding gains the derived id, file and line. The integration tests at upsert-script.vitest.ts lines 593 and 618 pin both behaviors. Fix: add one or two sentences after line 35 stating both behaviors.
